questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the language spoken was english, and that they had interesting courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: This was very difficult, which sometimes made the exchange more of a frustration and hassle than a positive and exciting experience.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was impossible to come in contact with my school through mail, even though I was well ahead of time. I had to go to the school to get help, which was also very difficult, only one person was able to help and she had very limited time.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Campus housing was way too expensive. No way I could have afforded that. But easy to apply for, if you wanted it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is way more difficult to meet people. If you don't live on campus with other students, then make sure to have roommates. A lot of people (coming from the same country og school back home) rent apartments together.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not very well explained to someone who doesn't know the system.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to apply for your courses before a certain deadline. But because I was an exchange student, I was not allowed/able to apply for any courses without an acceptance from the professor of that course, which was impossible to get, because they never answered.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Only one person were able to help with this problem, but she was not able to be reached through email.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: A lot of the courses i wanted to take, i was not able to get, because requisitions was required. But i was able to get my second choices.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be in really good time. And don't stress too much if you don't come through. Just meet up at the school when you arrive, and explain your situation and they will sort it out for you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had both level 300, 400 and 500 courses, and I think level 300 and 400 was pretty easy, especially level 300 was under my level of knowledge.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was pretty much the same. Mostly lectures. But better at referring what we learned to the exam, and how to use it, and practicing this.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sport psychology
Nutrition and wellness
Adapted physic activity
Sleep mechanisms and behaviour

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sleep mechanisms and behaviour was a really interesting course, but also a difficult one. 
Nutrition and wellness was also a good course, but quite easy.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I went on a lot of spontanous trips, and these were very costly, but also woth it.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping is very expensive in Canada.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You have to be fast, because the spots gets taken before you as an exchange student even realise it exits.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was an outdoor club, but not manny events were hold, and the ones that were hold, you didn't really hear about. I think there was quite a lot of social events in different forms, but you don't really hear about them unless you live on campus with the other students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The frosh events before the semester seems to be important to be a part of.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips. Rent a car and take small trips. Explore the city and their cafees. Stick to fun in the weekend and schoolwork during the week - you won't regret that! (it is the fun you will remember afterwards and look back at)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Become a part of a sport. Or live on campus with student housing.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That everything, especially administrative stuff, was only available in french.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The school system, especially exams, were way more functional and relevant.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't stress before arrival, it will sort itself out when you get there. 
Be quick to become a part of sport clubs or other trips.
Don't stress about reading all of the lecture material. Most of the times, it covers more or less the same.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about school. There is a lot of reading material, and it is impossible to read it all, and you will do just fine anyways. I was constantly behind, because i prioritized taking trips, and did just fine. Remember to also experience the area/country. It will always work out in the end.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Taking trips and experiencing the country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To balance school, exploring and social life. It is very intense to juggle all of these things at the same time, and it is just very different than back home. But just do it. Don't be afraid to have a busy schedule, you won't regret it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Put on the 'yes'-hat.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
